title: Dark-Store Picking and Packing QC
summary: A camera at the packing station checks each tote against the order before the bag is sealed, catching wrong variants, missing items and near-expiry stock, and keeps an image per order.

seo.title: Dark-Store Picking and Packing QC with AI | VipraTech
seo.description: Packing-station cameras check quick commerce orders against the pick list, flag wrong variants, missing items and near-expiry stock, and store evidence.

problem.intro: Quick commerce dark stores pick and pack an order in a few minutes, with no time for a second check. Toned milk instead of full cream, a 500 g pack instead of 1 kg or a missing item becomes a complaint, a refund and sometimes a lost customer.

pain_points.title: Wrong variants and missing items
pain_points.detail: Look-alike packs, sizes and flavours are easy to mix up at speed, and each mistake turns into a refund or a re-delivery.

pain_points.title: Near-expiry stock reaching customers
pain_points.detail: Dairy, bread and fresh items close to their date get picked during rush hours, leading to complaints and food-safety risk.

pain_points.title: No evidence for complaints
pain_points.detail: When a customer reports a missing item, support has no record of what went into the bag and often refunds by default.

pain_points.title: Speed leaves no room for checks
pain_points.detail: A manual second check at the packing station would slow every order, so it is skipped.

solution.overview: We build a packing-station check around an overhead camera above the tote or bag area. As the packer places items, the model identifies each product and compares it with the order lines from your WMS: right SKU, right variant, right count. Where the date is visible, it reads the expiry and applies your category shelf-life rule. If everything matches, the packer seals and dispatches as usual. If something is missing, extra or uncertain, the screen shows exactly which line to recheck. Every order gets an image linked to its order ID, which support can open when a complaint arrives.
capabilities: Identifies products in the tote and matches them to order lines by SKU, variant and count
Reads printed expiry dates where visible and applies your minimum shelf-life rules by category
Flags damaged, leaking or crushed packs for replacement before sealing
Shows the packer which line to recheck without stopping the station
Stores an image per order, linked to the order ID, for complaint handling
Store dashboards of mismatch types by SKU, shift and picker

workflow.title: Load the order
workflow.detail: The packer scans the order or tote, and the station pulls order lines from the WMS.

workflow.title: Capture the tote
workflow.detail: The overhead camera captures items as they are placed in the packing area.

workflow.title: Match items to the order
workflow.detail: The model identifies each product and compares SKU, variant, count and visible expiry with the order.

workflow.title: Packer rechecks flags
workflow.detail: Mismatches and uncertain items appear on screen for the packer to fix or confirm.

workflow.title: Seal and dispatch
workflow.detail: Once every line matches or is confirmed, the bag is sealed and handed to the rider.

workflow.title: Keep evidence and report
workflow.detail: The image is stored against the order ID, and mismatch data feeds store dashboards.

layers.name: Evidence and support

Support console view by order ID

inputs: Order lines and tote IDs from the WMS
Product images for the dark store assortment
Overhead camera images at the packing station
Customer complaint tickets referencing order IDs
outputs: Match or recheck prompt per order on the packer screen
Image per order linked to the order ID
Mismatch dashboard by store, SKU, shift and picker
Evidence view for support agents handling complaints
human_in_the_loop: Packers resolve every flagged line before sealing, and shift leads decide substitutions. Support agents decide refunds using the order image; the system provides evidence and does not approve or deny refunds.
integrations: Customer support platform such as Freshdesk or Zendesk
Product information or catalogue system for reference images
guardrails: Time budget per check so the station keeps its pace
Manual fallback when the camera or model is unavailable
Uncertain items always shown to the packer, never silently passed
Camera framed on the packing area, not on staff faces
Order images kept only for the agreed retention period
compliance_notes: Expiry checks help evidence FSSAI expectations that food sold online reaches customers with adequate remaining shelf life.
Images exclude staff faces and are kept only as long as complaint handling needs, in line with the DPDP Act 2023.

pilot.scope: Two or three packing stations in one dark store, covering the store's highest-volume categories, with post-pack audits as the benchmark.
deliverables: Recognition model for the pilot assortment
Packer screen and order image store
Accuracy report against post-pack audits and complaints

what_we_measure.how: Flags compared with errors found in post-pack audits of the same orders.
Flags the packer confirmed as correct, checked against audit samples.
Packing duration from WMS timestamps, with and without the check.
Share of missing or wrong item complaints on pilot orders where support could open the order image.

faqs.a: It is designed to run while the packer works, not as an extra step. We measure packing time from WMS timestamps during the pilot and tune camera position and screen prompts so the station keeps pace.

faqs.q: How does it handle new SKUs, which we add every week?
faqs.a: New products are added from catalogue images and a few photos taken at the station. Until a SKU is learned, the system marks it as unverified rather than guessing.

faqs.q: Can it read expiry dates on every product?
faqs.a: Only where the date faces the camera. Many dates are printed on the back or bottom, so expiry checks work best for categories where packers place the date face up, such as dairy and bread.
That is your choice. Most teams use it internally for complaint handling first, and some share it with the customer when a complaint is disputed.
